hero.title: Mauryan Empire: Social Stratification
hero.description: An analytical study of the rigid social structure, Megasthenes' seven-fold classification, and the status of women and slavery during the Mauryan period.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key phases of the Mauryan social evolution.

cards.details: Chandragupta Maurya establishes the empire, institutionalizing Kautilyan social norms.
Integration of Dhamma, influencing social ethics and the status of different varna groups.

items.title: P.F.S.H.O.S.C
items.phrase: Philosophers, Farmers, Soldiers, Herdsmen, Overseers, Sabhas/Councillors, Craftsmen.
items.decryption: Remember the specific order listed by Megasthenes, as he ignored the traditional Vedic Varna system.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming Megasthenes' 7-class system replaced the Varna system; it was a contemporary observer's perspective, not a legal reality.
Believing slavery did not exist; Kautilya mentions slaves (Dasas) clearly, though their condition differed from Greek slavery.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Social Groups

  • Megasthenes' 7 Classes
  • Brahmins and Shramanas
  • Status of Women

Labour

  • Slaves (Dasas/Ahilakas)
  • Hired laborers (Karmakaras)
  • Artisans

Mauryan Social Hierarchy

  • Varna System: Kautilya supports the Varna-ashrama dharma; social stability was prioritized.
  • Megasthenes' Observations: He divided society into 7 classes: Philosophers, Husbandmen, Shepherds, Artisans/Traders, Soldiers, Overseers, and Councillors.
  • Women: Possessed Stridhana; some worked as royal guards and spies.
  • Slavery: Kautilya details legal aspects of slavery, distinguishing it from Greco-Roman models.
ClassRole
PhilosophersIntellectuals/Brahmins
FarmersLargest population
SoldiersState-maintained army

practiceQuestions.q: Who wrote the account 'Indica', which provides a detailed description of Indian society and social stratification during the Mauryan period?
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. He wrote 'Indica', where he famously classified Indian society into seven castes.

practiceQuestions.q: According to Megasthenes' account in 'Indica', how many classes or castes was Indian society divided into?
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes divided Indian society into seven occupational categories: Philosophers, Farmers, Herdsmen/Hunters, Artisans/Traders, Soldiers, Overseers, and Counselors/Assessors.

practiceQuestions.q: In Kautilya's Arthashastra, what is the term used to refer to legally recognized slaves?
practiceQuestions.sol: In the Arthashastra, 'Dasa' specifically refers to slaves, whose legal rights and manumission processes are elaborately discussed by Kautilya, setting the Mauryan empire apart from classical slavery systems like Greece.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following groups formed the largest segment of the population according to Megasthenes' seven-fold classification?
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes noted that farmers constituted the most numerous and vital section of the Indian population, as they were exempted from fighting and devoted themselves entirely to tillage.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the term used in Mauryan administration for women who worked as personal bodyguards and security guards for the King?
practiceQuestions.sol: Greek accounts and the Arthashastra mention armed women bodyguards, often referred to as archers and guards recruited from abroad or trained locally, akin to Amazons, protecting the monarch.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of Mauryan social structure, what does the term 'Anuloma' marriage refer to?
opts: Marriage between a higher caste man and a lower caste woman
Marriage between a higher caste woman and a lower caste man
Marriage outside the caste system entirely
practiceQuestions.sol: Anuloma was a hypergamous form of marriage where a man from a higher varna married a woman from a lower varna. It was socially permissible though regulated.

practiceQuestions.q: Which category in Megasthenes' seven-fold caste system was numerically smallest but held the highest prestige and influence in spiritual matters?
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes placed philosophers (Brahmarnas and Shramanas) at the top of his list because of their wisdom, despite their small number, and noted their exemption from taxation and manual labor.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the legal provision regarding the emancipation of slaves in the Mauryan period as per Kautilya's Arthashastra?
opts: Slaves could never be freed under any circumstances.
Slaves could purchase their freedom by paying an equivalent ransom.
Only the King could grant freedom to state slaves.
Slaves were automatically freed after working for one year.
practiceQuestions.sol: Kautilya laid down that a slave could earn their freedom by paying an equivalent amount of ransom (price). Additionally, master-slave relations were legally regulated to prevent physical abuse.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Mauryan administrative and social terminology, what did the term 'Nishkriya' or 'Anishkriya' women signify?
opts: Women who were confined to domestic life and household duties (Anishkriya)
Women who held high ministerial posts
Female soldiers in the royal army
Women ascetics who renounced the world
practiceQuestions.sol: Kautilya refers to women who were exempted from leaving their homes or going out to courts (Anishkriya - women whose movements were restricted to the home, or women free from outside work), while 'Nishkriya' often denoted women of high seclusion.

practiceQuestions.q: What status did 'Ganikas' (courtesans) hold in Mauryan society according to the Arthashastra?
opts: They were completely ostracized and outlawed.
They were state-recognized, highly respected professionals under official superintendence.
They were treated as slaves with no economic rights.
They were exclusively employed as foreign spies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Ganikas in the Mauryan state held a secure and officially regulated status. They paid taxes to the state, enjoyed high social standing due to their accomplishments, and were overseen by a state official called Ganikadhyaksha.

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Megasthenes misinterpret the Indian social structure into seven castes instead of the traditional four varnas?
opts: He deliberately fabricated data to please the Greek emperor.
He confused occupational sub-castes and professions with the theoretical varna system.
The varna system had completely collapsed during the Mauryan period.
He only interacted with the untouchable communities of Pataliputra.
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes was an outsider observer who mistook occupational categories (like farmers, shepherds, artisans) for immutable castes, completely missing the underlying philosophical framework of the four varnas.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the economic policy of the Mauryan state, particularly extensive land clearance and agrarian expansion, impact social stratification?
opts: It led to the complete abolition of the caste system in newly settled areas.
It resulted in the deployment of Shudra laborers and slaves to cultivate crown lands, deepening economic stratification.
It elevated all peasants to the status of Brahmins.
It made slavery completely obsolete throughout the empire.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mauryan state brought vast tracts of virgin land under cultivation through state-sponsored agricultural settlements (Sitadhyaksha). These lands were worked upon by Shudra laborers and slaves, reinforcing their lower economic and social standing.

practiceQuestions.q: What was a significant structural difference between Roman/Greek slavery and Mauryan slavery as depicted in the Arthashastra?
opts: Mauryan slavery was harsher and formed the core of industrial production.
Mauryan slavery was relatively mild, and slaves could own property and engage in legal transactions.
Mauryan slaves were exclusively used for gladiator fights.
There were no legal laws governing the treatment of slaves in the Mauryan empire.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the Greco-Roman world where slaves were chattel with virtually no rights, Mauryan slavery was integrated into domestic and agrarian production with specific legal protections against cruelty, the right to acquire property, and avenues for manumission.

practiceQuestions.q: How did Ashoka's Dhamma policy attempt to modify interpersonal and social relations within the Mauryan social hierarchy?
opts: By legally enforcing the total dismantling of caste barriers
By promoting ethical behavior, respect for elders, kindness to slaves and servants, and religious tolerance across all strata
By granting absolute political power exclusively to Buddhist monks
By abolishing taxation for all lower-caste peasants
practiceQuestions.sol: Ashoka's Dhamma did not abolish the caste system or structural stratification; instead, it promoted moral restraint, humanitarian treatment of slaves and servants, respect for teachers, and non-violence to ease the tensions within the hierarchical society.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the socio-economic impact of the proliferation of crafts and guilds (Shrenis) during the Mauryan era?
opts: It caused the complete disappearance of urban centers.
It led to the crystallization of artisanal communities into specialized sub-castes (Jatis).
It forced all artisans to become agricultural serfs.
It subordinated all guilds directly to foreign merchant control.
practiceQuestions.sol: The growth of specialized crafts and professional guilds (Shrenis) during the Mauryan period contributed significantly to the transformation of occupational groups into hereditary sub-castes (Jatis) within the broader varna framework.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the status of women regarding property rights (Stridhana) during the Mauryan period. Which of the following best reflects the legal framework?
opts: Women had no rights to hold any movable or immovable property.
Women were entitled to 'Stridhana' (gifts given at marriage), over which they had independent financial control.
All property owned by women automatically reverted to the state upon marriage.
Women could only inherit property if they had no male siblings.
practiceQuestions.sol: According to the Arthashastra, women possessed independent control over their Stridhana (gifts, jewelry, and maintenance received during marriage), providing a degree of economic security within a patriarchal structure.

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Kautilya permit women to engage in economic activities outside the home, such as spinning and weaving in state workshops?
opts: To dismantle the patriarchal family system entirely
To harness cheap female labor—especially widows, destitute women, and courtesans—for state revenue generation.
To promote gender equality in political governance
To replace male soldiers in the royal military
practiceQuestions.sol: Kautilya's state controlled textile production through state workshops (Sutradhyaksha) and employed vulnerable women (widows, orphans, disabled, retired courtesans) to work for wages, maximizing state revenue through mobilized female labor.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the territorial expansion of the Mauryan Empire affect its social fabric?
opts: It resulted in a homogenous, caste-free society across all conquered provinces.
It facilitated the spread of the Brahmanical varna-ashrama system into tribal and peripheral regions, leading to acculturation.
It caused the complete collapse of trade networks and de-urbanization.
It forced nomadic tribes to migrate out of the Indian subcontinent.
practiceQuestions.sol: The expansion of the Mauryan imperial administration brought tribal populations and non-Vedic groups into contact with the Gangetic core culture, initiating the process of Sanskritization and incorporation into the lower strata of the varna hierarchy.

practiceQuestions.q: What does the existence of diverse legal penalties based on varna in the Mauryan penal code (as seen in the Arthashastra) indicate about social stratification?
opts: That equality before the law was the foundational principle of Mauryan jurisprudence.
That the legal system institutionalized inequality, prescribing harsher punishments for lower varnas and lenient ones for higher varnas.
That judicial punishments were completely arbitrary and unrelated to social status.
That Brahmins were subjected to capital punishment more frequently than Shudras.
practiceQuestions.sol: Kautilya's legal codes reflected the Brahmanical social order where the severity of punishments for crimes (especially defamation, assault, and theft) varied according to the varna of the offender and the victim, favoring upper varnas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements best evaluates the role of slavery in the Mauryan economy compared to contemporary Mediterranean societies?
opts: Mauryan economy was entirely dependent on chattel slavery for agricultural and mineral production, mirroring Rome.
While slavery existed and was utilized in state farms and mines, wage labor (Karmakaras) and peasant farming played a far more dominant economic role.
Slavery was legally prohibited and practically non-existent in the Mauryan Empire.
Slaves were the exclusive ruling class controlling the political apparatus of the Mauryan state.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike ancient Greece or Rome, where slave labor formed the backbone of the entire economy, the Mauryan economy was primarily sustained by free peasant proprietors (tax-paying cultivators) and wage laborers, with slaves playing a supplementary role.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Megasthenes' account of Indian society during the Mauryan period:
1. He noted that Indian society was divided into seven classes based on occupation rather than the traditional four-fold varna system.
2. According to him, slaves did not exist in India at all.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Megasthenes classified Indian society into seven functional occupational groups. Statement 2 is incorrect because while Megasthenes claimed that all Indians were free and that slavery did not exist in India (misinterpreting the mild nature of Indian domestic slavery compared to Greek chattel slavery), other contemporary texts like the Arthashastra clearly document the existence of slaves.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the position of women in the Mauryan period:
1. Women were completely barred from any form of economic participation outside the household.
2. The Arthashastra mentions the employment of female bodyguards and secret agents by the king.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because women, especially widows, distressed women, and courtesans, actively participated in state-run workshops in spinning, weaving, and agriculture. Statement 2 is correct: Kautilya's Arthashastra details the use of armed female bodyguards (Amazonian guards) and female spies (agent-provocateurs) for royal security.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding slavery in the Mauryan empire:
1. Slaves had absolute lack of legal rights and could be executed by their masters at will.
2. Kautilya's Arthashastra outlines rules under which slaves could purchase their freedom and protects them from physical abuse.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because masters did not have the right to arbitrary execution or severe abuse; doing so invited heavy fines by the state. Statement 2 is correct as Kautilya provided legal provisions for slaves to buy their freedom and penalized masters who abused slave women or children.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Megasthenes' classification of the Indian population:
1. He ranked philosophers at the highest level of social prestige despite their small numerical strength.
2. He explicitly mentioned that the warrior class (soldiers) outnumbered all other classes in the empire.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Megasthenes placed philosophers (Brahmins and Shramanas) first because of their intellectual and spiritual status. Statement 2 is incorrect because farmers, not soldiers, constituted the most numerous section of the population according to Megasthenes.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the varna system during the Mauryan period:
1. The rigidity of the varna system was completely neutralized by Buddhist patronage under Ashoka.
2. The emergence of numerous mixed castes (Varnasankara) through inter-varna marriages was acknowledged in Mauryan legal texts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: while Ashoka's Dhamma preached social harmony, mutual respect, and tolerance, it did not dismantle or neutralize the varna system. Statement 2 is correct: texts like the Arthashastra recognize and regulate the social status of various mixed castes (Varnasankara) arising from Anuloma and Pratiloma marriages.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the institution of 'Ganikas' (courtesans) in the Mauryan state:
1. They were illegal outcasts who operated underground.
2. They were registered with a state superintendent (Ganikadhyaksha) and contributed substantial revenue to the state exchequer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Ganikas were not outcasts; they held a recognized and prestigious profession. Statement 2 is correct: they were under the direct supervision of a state official (Ganikadhyaksha), paid taxes, performed cultural functions, and often served as intelligence agents for the state.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic basis of social classes in the Mauryan period:
1. The state controlled vast agricultural lands (Sita lands) tilled exclusively by the royal family members.
2. Wage laborers (Karmakaras) and agricultural slaves formed the bedrock of the labor force utilized in state-managed economic enterprises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Sita lands were cultivated not by royal family members, but by Shudra laborers, prisoners, and slaves under the supervision of the Sitadhyaksha. Statement 2 is correct: wage laborers and slaves constituted the primary workforce for state farms, mines, and factories.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ashoka's Edicts and their reflection on social stratification:
1. Ashoka's Rock Edicts explicitly command the abolition of the Brahmanical varna system throughout the empire.
2. Rock Edicts emphasize proper treatment, courtesy, and humane behavior toward slaves and servants (Dasa-bhrataka).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Ashoka's edicts do not abolish the varna system; rather, they urge respect for Brahmins and Shramanas alike. Statement 2 is correct: multiple edicts (such as Major Rock Edict IX and XI) repeatedly stress proper and compassionate conduct towards slaves and servants.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal and social status of marriage and divorce in the Mauryan period:
1. Divorce (Moksha) was legally recognized under specific conditions in the Arthashastra.
2. Widows were prohibited from remarrying under any circumstances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Kautilya's Arthashastra permits dissolution of marriage (moksha) under mutual enmity or specific hardships. Statement 2 is incorrect because widow remarriage (Niyoga or remarriage provisions) was legally permitted under certain circumstances in Mauryan jurisprudence.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the occupational division in Megasthenes' Indica:
1. Artisans and tradesmen were placed in a distinct category separate from farmers and philosophers.
2. Intermarriage between the seven classes described by Megasthenes was strictly permitted and freely practiced without restriction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Megasthenes listed artisans, ship-builders, and tradesmen as a separate group (the fourth class). Statement 2 is incorrect because Megasthenes explicitly noted strict rules against intermarriage between these classes, indicating that occupational boundaries were rigid.
